messages:
olivia: CI red on linux-x86_64 (action/runtime): `RetryManagerTests::backoff_jitter_on_contention` failed 1/20 in nightly. Can someone kick a rerun?
ci-bot: Test failure detected: RetryManagerTests::backoff_jitter_on_contention — job: linux-x86_64-nightly — failed at 1745567889 — logs uploaded to: https://ci.internal/runs/12345/logs
mateo: re-ran locally once on my workstation, couldn't repro. can we try a rerun with different seeds? @olivia do we have the failing seed in the log? :thinking:
olivia: log shows seed=927413 but the failure is timing sensitive, looks like two retries overlapped and assertion on max_backoff hit. snippet: ```RetryManager: scheduling retry backoff=120ms, jitter=+8ms
...
RetryManager: scheduling retry backoff=120ms, jitter=-5ms
Assertion failed: total_backoff <= configured_max_backoff (150ms)```
sasha: hmm, that sounds like a race where jitter pushes the second retry beyond the ceiling. Could be an off-by-one when clamping. I'll take a quick look. If anyone's able to bisect, maybe narrow to a PR range that touched backoff logic last week (PRs: #1124, #1129).
noah: I can run the flaky-test detector across the last 200 builds to see frequency and if it correlates to cpu/machine type. Pointing to linux-x86_64 only now?
olivia: only in linux-x86_64-nightly so far, mac & windows green. Frequency ~5% in last 2 weeks per ci summary.
mateo: ok doing a rerun now: `./ci/rerun.sh 12345 --target RetryManagerTests::backoff_jitter_on_contention`
ci-bot: Rerun queued by mateo for run 12345. New run id 12345-rerun-1.
ci-bot: Rerun finished: 12345-rerun-1 — PASSED
olivia: thanks, mateo. passing on rerun doesn't help bisecting though. any ideas for deterministic repro?
sasha: two things to try: 1) add a tiny sleep before clamping to attempt to reproduce the overlap, 2) instrument the clamping code to log pre/post values + thread id. If we can reproduce locally with stress-ng or workload harness we can bisect easier.
noah: I ran the frequency scan — spikes line up with high-concurrency runs (concurrent_jobs >= 48). Most failures on machines with 32-core VMs. I'll spin a stress run with `--concurrency 64` and seed list [927413, 431224, 118990].
mateo: if we suspect clamping math, quick patch suggestion: ensure clamp uses unsigned math and saturating min. i.e. `backoff = min(config_max, base + jitter)` not `if (base + jitter > config_max) base = config_max` which can race.
olivia: @sasha if you want, I'll push a small debug build with extra logs to a throwaway branch and point CI at it. quick yes/no? :+1:
sasha: yes please, that'll speed it up. also add thread id to the log lines.
olivia: done: pushed branch `olivia/debug/retry-clamp-logs` and triggered nightly: https://ci.internal/runs/12346
ci-bot: New run 12346 triggered by olivia on branch olivia/debug/retry-clamp-logs — job linux-x86_64-nightly
ci-bot: run 12346 completed — FAIL — same test — logs: https://ci.internal/runs/12346/logs
noah: grabbing logs...
noah: log excerpt shows: ```thread=52 base=120 jitter=8 pre_clamp=128 post_clamp=128 config_max=150
thread=53 base=120 jitter=-5 pre_clamp=115 post_clamp=115 config_max=150
...
thread=52 scheduled_at=10000ms thread=53 scheduled_at=10025ms assertion total_backoff<=150 failed```
sasha: interesting — pre_clamp values below max, so clamp not tripping. The assertion is on total_backoff across retries, not per-retry. maybe we miscount retries accumulating two overlapping retry windows. that could explain sum > max.
mateo: can we add a guard: if (sum_of_active_backoffs > config_max) log stack traces of retry owners. if it repros we can identify source threads.
olivia: added extra logging + stack traces to the branch; re-triggering quick job (12347).
ci-bot: run 12347 queued...
ci-bot: run 12347 finished — FAIL — same test — logs: https://ci.internal/runs/12347/logs
noah: logs now include owner stacks: shows RetryToken from connection_manager::Worker::run() and another from kv_prefetch::Prefetcher::on_evict(). Looks like two subsystems schedule retries for the same logical request concurrently.
sasha: aha — two different components retrying the same high-level operation. we probably intended only one retry coordinator per request. That explains sum-of-backoffs > max.
mateo: PR idea: add request-scoped retry guard token (idempotent) so only one RetryManager handles backoff for that request. low-risk change, tests should catch regressions.
olivia: ok let's spec the change and pair on the PR. I'll create an issue and assign. quick plan: 1) add request retry id, 2) ensure existing tests include simulated double-schedulers, 3) add a regression test that asserts total_backoff <= config_max even under concurrent scheduling.
sasha: sounds good. I can open the PR and include your debug instrumentation to show before/after.
noah: leaving a note: if we can't reduce probability to zero, add a CI alert to rerun flaky occurrences automatically and tag owners.
olivia: created issue #1789 and draft PR 11877. assigning to @sasha and @mateo for review. thanks all for quick triage :shipit:
